comment: Every test failure this repository currently expects, and why.
It exists because a step that is already red absorbs the next failure without trace.
TestGenerateCatalogIdempotent was red on main for two merges, inside a step red for the
ratchet; TestFirehoseSnowflakeSecretAndPersistentBuffer failed once inside the same step
and was invisible for the same reason. Neither was hidden cleverly. Both were hidden by a
scripts/known-red.sh reads a `go test` run and says which of its failures are on this list
and which are not. It does NOT make anything pass: every entry here is still a red test and
still fails its step. What changes is that the first line of the output says whether the red
is the one expected or a new one -- which is the whole difference between a gate and a colour.
An entry may be added only with a reason a reader can check, and removed the moment the test
goes green. TestKnownRedIsDeclaredHonestly enforces both halves: every entry must name a test
that exists in the tree and carry a non-empty reason.

expected.why: Deliberate, and the point of the ratchet. The baseline is the PRE-DRIFT target, not a floor to raise: two packs -- azure/blobs and railway/graphql -- were added after it was cut, so the tree exceeds it until both are extracted. Goes green by deleting those packs, never by running `ratchet -write`.
The other half of the same statement: ratchet.json is deliberately stale relative to the tree, for exactly as long as TestRatchetNotExceeded is red, and for the same two packs.

Five services are served with no generated model. Three are AWS services whose Smithy model the receiver cannot yet ingest (aws.elastictranscoder, aws.lookoutmetrics, aws.qldb); two are the hand-written packs still to be extracted (azure.blobs, railway.graphql). The count may only fall.

An EQUIVALENT mutant: no test can kill it, because the code it rewrites has no observable effect. The S3 pack reads the query string in two places, and `delimiter` is hydrated by the first, so the per-operation fallback the mutant rewrites is unreachable. Recorded in full as C36. Goes away with the second read, not with a new test.
Equivalent for the same reason as -ignore-http-delimiter: `key-marker` is in the hydration block, so the fallback that names it is dead code. C36.
Equivalent for an unrelated reason. It flips `maxUploads < 1` to `< 0`, and those differ only at zero -- three lines below a `maxUploads == 0` that has already rewritten zero to 1000. C36.
